title: The nine reminders
hook: Marcus lists nine things to recall when offended: we're made for each other, they act from beliefs, we err too (Meditations 11.18)

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was Phocion, the general who asked his son to bear no grudge. Your line was theirs, and mine.

Someone offends you, and the old script starts running: how dare they, who do they think they are, wait till I tell everyone. Marcus wrote a different script. It's a long entry, numbered first, second, third, like a pilot's checklist before takeoff. He wrote it to read when someone offended him, a list to run before the reply goes out.
screen: `HOW DARE THEY.` → `A NUMBERED CHECKLIST.` → `THE NINE REMINDERS.`

segments.voice: First, about them. One: we're made for one another. Two: think what these people are like at the table, in bed, and what beliefs are driving them. Three: if they're right, don't complain; if they're wrong, it's unwillingly, out of ignorance. No soul, Marcus says, is willingly cut off from the truth. Second, about you. Four: you do plenty of wrong yourself, and even when you don't, you have the tendency, held back only by fear or concern for your reputation. Five: you don't even know for certain that they're doing wrong; many things are done for reasons you can't see. Six: when you're furious, remember that life is a moment, and soon we'll all be laid out. Third, about the anger. Seven: it isn't their acts that disturb us; those live in them. It's our own judgments. Take away the judgment that it's terrible, and the anger goes with it. Eight: our anger and grief hurt us more than the things that caused them. Fourth, the last. Nine: kindness is invincible, if it's real, not a fake smile or an act. What can the most violent person do if you stay kind, and at the very moment they try to harm you, gently say: no, my child, we were made for something else; you won't harm me, you're harming yourself, my child. Then Marcus adds a tenth, as a gift, he says, from the leader of the Muses: to expect bad people not to do wrong is madness.
screen: `ONE TO THREE: KIN, BELIEFS, IGNORANCE.` · `FOUR TO SIX: ME TOO, UNSURE, BRIEF.` · `SEVEN AND EIGHT: MY JUDGMENT, MY ANGER.` · `NINE: KINDNESS IS INVINCIBLE.` · then, large: `NINE REMINDERS.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person who offended you recently, and run the nine slowly: we're made for each other; they act from their beliefs; if they're wrong, it's unwilling; I've done the same; I can't be sure; life is short; it's my judgment that hurts; my anger hurts more; kindness can't be beaten. Let each one land for a breath, and notice which one loosens the knot.
My child. Marcus's gentle answer to real harm: no, my child, we were made for something else; you're only harming yourself. Today's word.
Your line: nine reminders. Even three of them can slow the reply. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some readers of the Meditations copy out the nine reminders and reread them when someone has offended them, often before replying.

chat.says: A kid at school insulted me. Why should I stay kind to him?
options: Marcus says real kindness can't be beaten, and whoever harms you harms himself most.
Marcus says stay kind only until he apologizes, and then you can let it go.
Marcus says smile and stay polite outside, even if you're furious inside.

Marcus.meaning: Marcus Aurelius, Roman emperor who wrote the Meditations to himself

my child.meaning: Marcus's gentle way of addressing someone trying to harm him

leader of the Muses.meaning: Apollo, the Greek god who leads the goddesses of the arts

notes: 11.18 paraphrased in full: (1) relation to men, made for one another (with the ram/bull image omitted); (2) what they are at table, in bed, compelled by opinions; (3) if right, no complaint; if not, involuntarily, in ignorance; (4) you too do wrong, or have the disposition, restrained by cowardice or reputation; (5) you don't know they are doing wrong; (6) life is a moment, we are soon laid out; (7) it's our opinions, not their acts, that disturb us; (8) anger and vexation cause more pain than the acts; (9) benevolence is invincible if genuine; 'Not so, my child...'; tenth gift from the leader of the Muses (Apollo Musagetes).
